Description: Coil spring (circular wire, mean radius 10, wire radius 2, so the wire occupies the radial band 8..12, z from -2 to 26) and a coaxial cylinder of radius 12, z from 0 to 24. Unlike the other tangency cases the two bodies REALLY OVERLAP: the wire lies completely inside the cylinder radially and only grazes its lateral face at exactly r=12. Only the two wire ends stick out below z=0 and above z=24.
Expected: union: ONE solid (the bodies share a large common volume, so this is not a mere-touching case), volume V(coil) + V(cylinder) - V(intersect) = 2368.661 + 10857.340 - 2284.897 = 10941.104. intersect: the part of the coil inside the cylinder, about 2284.9.
Status: intersect is CORRECT (2284.8965, reproducible over three runs - it is not equal to operand a, so the empty-intersection bug does not apply here). union returns TWO solids instead of one.
Actual: solid.boolean union returns a solid[] with count 2, reproducibly over three runs. Rendering the result looks geometrically right (cylinder with the coil merged in, wire ends protruding at both ends), so this looks like a result-splitting/bookkeeping issue rather than wrong geometry. Note: in the build before the tangency fix this same pair returned a SINGLE solid from union (volume 10950.97, measured with a correctly oriented coil), so this may be a regression - but that comparison is not perfectly controlled, since the coil volume itself changed slightly with the fix.
Note: Because the union result is a solid[], inspect.properties cannot report its volume ('Property Volume not found on type List<Solid>'), which is why no union volume is listed above.
